name: Maasai Mara 3-Day Safari
description: Experience Kenya's crown jewel on a three-day safari through the Maasai Mara National Reserve. Witness vast herds of wildebeest, zebra, and gazelle roaming golden plains patrolled by big cats and elephants. During the Great Migration season (July-October), over two million animals cross the Mara River in one of nature's most breathtaking spectacles.
shortDescription: Three-day game drive adventure through Kenya's iconic Maasai Mara, home to the Big Five and the Great Migration.
highlights: Big Five game drives across the Mara's sweeping plains
Mara River crossing during the Great Migration (Jul-Oct)
Exclusive lodge or tented camp accommodation
Sundowner cocktails on the savanna at golden hour
Expert Maasai naturalist guides with decades of experience
notes: Budget safaris use shared 4x4 vehicles and basic camps; luxury tiers include private vehicles, fly-in transfers, and all-inclusive lodges. Book 3-6 months ahead for peak migration season (July-October).

name: Amboseli Safari Experience
description: Set against the magnificent backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro, Amboseli National Park is famous for its large elephant herds and sweeping panoramas. Game drives here offer front-row views of elephants silhouetted against Africa's highest peak, alongside buffalo, hippo, and an impressive array of birdlife in the park's seasonal wetlands.
shortDescription: Safari through Amboseli with stunning Kilimanjaro views and some of Kenya's largest elephant herds.
bestSeason: June to October (dry season, best visibility of Kilimanjaro)
highlights: Massive elephant herds with Mount Kilimanjaro as backdrop
Observation Hill panoramic viewpoint over the park
Wetland birdwatching with 400+ species recorded
Maasai cultural visits in surrounding group ranches
Sunrise and sunset game drives for optimal photography
notes: Kilimanjaro is best viewed in the early morning before clouds build. The park can be combined with Tsavo for a longer safari circuit. Afternoon haze is common. Plan photography for dawn.

name: Tsavo Safari Adventure
description: Explore one of the world's largest wildlife sanctuaries spanning Tsavo East and Tsavo West together, covering over 20,000 square kilometres of red-earth wilderness. Tsavo East's open plains host vast herds of red-dusted elephants, while Tsavo West's volcanic landscapes harbour the crystal-clear Mzima Springs, where hippos and crocodiles glide through underwater viewing chambers.
shortDescription: Vast wilderness safari across Tsavo East and West featuring red elephants, volcanic landscapes, and Mzima Springs.
bestSeason: June to October (dry season, animals concentrate at water sources)
highlights: Famous red-dusted elephants of Tsavo East
Mzima Springs underwater hippo and crocodile viewing
Shetani Lava Flow volcanic landscapes in Tsavo West
Man-eaters of Tsavo historical sites
Lugard Falls and the Galana River game viewing
notes: Tsavo East is flatter and drier with better elephant sightings; Tsavo West is hillier and more scenic. The parks are conveniently located between Nairobi and Mombasa, making them ideal for safari-and-beach combinations.

name: Samburu Wildlife Safari
description: Journey to the remote semi-arid landscapes of Samburu National Reserve to encounter the 'Samburu Special Five': Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and Beisa oryx. These species are found nowhere else in Kenya's popular safari circuit. The Ewaso Ng'iro River bisects the reserve, drawing dense concentrations of wildlife to its palm-lined banks.
shortDescription: Discover rare wildlife species in the stunning semi-arid landscapes of northern Kenya's Samburu Reserve.
bestSeason: July to October (dry season, best game viewing)
highlights: The Samburu Special Five: unique northern species
Ewaso Ng'iro River game viewing from camp verandas
Leopard sightings: Samburu has one of the highest densities
Samburu warrior-led cultural experiences
Fewer crowds than the Mara for an intimate bush feel
notes: Samburu is approximately 5-6 hours' drive from Nairobi or a short charter flight. Temperatures can exceed 35 °C. Light, breathable clothing and sun protection are essential. Best combined with Laikipia for a comprehensive northern Kenya circuit.

name: Lake Nakuru Safari
description: Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is renowned for its dramatic flamingo congregations and as a sanctuary for both black and white rhinos. The alkaline lake's shallow waters attract millions of lesser flamingos that paint the shoreline pink, while the surrounding acacia woodland provides habitat for leopard, lion, and Rothschild's giraffe.
shortDescription: Rhino sanctuary and flamingo spectacle at Lake Nakuru, a compact but wildlife-rich national park.
highlights: Millions of flamingos carpeting the alkaline lake shore
Black and white rhino sighting opportunities
Rothschild's giraffe: one of the most endangered subspecies
Baboon Cliff panoramic viewpoint over the lake
Compact park ideal for a one-day safari
notes: Flamingo numbers vary with water levels and algae bloom cycles. They may move to other Rift Valley lakes such as Bogoria. The park is just 2 hours from Nairobi, making it ideal for a day trip or overnight. Entry is $60 for non-residents.

name: Walking Safari (Conservancy)
description: Step out of the vehicle and into the African bush on a guided walking safari through a private conservancy. Led by armed rangers and expert trackers, these intimate foot patrols bring you face-to-face with the sights, sounds, and scents that a game drive can never capture. Learn from tracking elephant spoor to identifying medicinal plants used by local communities.
shortDescription: Guided bush walk through a private conservancy for an intimate, on-foot wildlife experience.
highlights: Track wildlife on foot with expert Maasai or Samburu guides
Learn bush survival skills and traditional plant identification
Intimate small-group experience (max 6-8 guests)
Close encounters with smaller wildlife missed from vehicles
Photography from unique ground-level perspectives
notes: Walking safaris are only permitted in conservancies, not in national parks/reserves. Minimum age typically 12-16 years depending on operator. A moderate level of fitness is required. Long trousers, closed shoes, and neutral-coloured clothing are mandatory.

name: Night Game Drive
description: Venture into the African night on a spotlight-equipped game drive to discover the elusive nocturnal world that remains hidden during the day. Night drives reveal leopards on the prowl, aardvarks emerging from burrows, bush babies leaping through the canopy, and the haunting calls of hyenas echoing across the plains.
shortDescription: Spotlight-guided nocturnal safari to encounter leopards, aardvarks, and other elusive night creatures.
highlights: Spot nocturnal predators: leopard, hyena, civet, and genet
Aardvark and pangolin sightings (rare but possible)
Bush baby and nightjar encounters in the canopy
Star-studded African sky far from city light pollution
A completely different perspective on the bush
notes: Night drives are not allowed in national parks. They are exclusive to private conservancies. A warm jacket is essential as temperatures drop significantly after dark. Red-filter spotlights are used to avoid disturbing the animals.

name: Photographic Safari
description: Designed for photography enthusiasts, these specialised safaris use custom-modified vehicles with swivel seats, bean-bag mounts, and pop-up roofs for unobstructed shooting angles. Expert photography guides position you for the best light and composition, with game drives timed around the golden hours of dawn and dusk when the African light is at its most dramatic.
shortDescription: Specialist safari in custom photography vehicles with expert guides, timed for optimal golden-hour light.
bestSeason: July to October (Great Migration, dry landscapes, clear light)
highlights: Custom photography vehicles with bean-bag mounts and USB charging
Expert photography guide for composition and wildlife behaviour tips
Extended golden-hour game drives (no rush back for meals)
Access to private conservancies with fewer vehicles
Post-processing workshops at camp during midday downtime
notes: Bring your own camera gear. Some operators offer lens rental. Download speeds at remote camps are limited, so bring sufficient memory cards. A 200-400mm telephoto lens is ideal for most wildlife photography. Some operators offer drone photography by special permit.

name: Meru National Park Safari
description: Follow in the footsteps of Joy and George Adamson at Meru National Park, the setting of the classic 'Born Free' story. This underrated gem offers lush landscapes of palm-fringed rivers, dense bush, and open grassland supporting all the Big Five. With a fraction of the visitor traffic found in more popular parks, Meru's remoteness is its greatest asset.
shortDescription: Uncrowded 'Born Free' country . lush riverine landscapes and all the Big Five at Meru National Park.
highlights: Born Free legacy . Elsa the lioness memorial and Adamson sites
Big Five sightings with very few other vehicles around
Thirteen rivers create lush, palm-fringed game-viewing corridors
White rhino sanctuary within the park
Diverse landscapes from grassland to riverine forest
notes: Meru is roughly 4 hours' drive northeast of Nairobi or accessible by charter flight. Roads inside the park can be rough, especially in the wet season. The park is being actively rehabilitated and wildlife numbers are increasing steadily.

name: Laikipia Conservancy Safari
description: The Laikipia Plateau is Kenya's conservation success story . a patchwork of private and community conservancies that together support the country's second-largest elephant population and highest density of endangered black rhinos. Safaris here go beyond standard game drives, offering walking safaris, horseback rides, camel treks, and night drives in a landscape of dramatic escarpments and sweeping highland plains.
shortDescription: Multi-activity safari on the Laikipia Plateau . walks, rides, night drives, and rhino conservation.
bestSeason: Year-round (no single peak . Laikipia is consistently excellent)
highlights: Highest black rhino density in East Africa
Multi-activity options: walk, ride, drive, and fly
Community conservancy model supporting local livelihoods
Night drives and walking safaris permitted (unlike national parks)
Dramatic Mt Kenya backdrop on clear days
notes: Laikipia conservancies are all-inclusive . rates typically cover accommodation, meals, drinks, conservancy fees, and activities. Most are accessed via light aircraft from Nairobi's Wilson Airport (45-60 min). Each conservancy has its own character and specialisation.

name: Snorkeling Watamu Marine Park
description: Glide over vibrant coral gardens in Watamu Marine National Park, one of Kenya's oldest and most pristine marine protected areas. The park's shallow reefs teem with parrotfish, angelfish, moray eels, and sea turtles, all visible in crystal-clear water just metres from the shore. Glass-bottom boats ferry snorkelers to the best coral heads.
shortDescription: Snorkel over pristine coral reefs teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles in Watamu Marine Park.
bestSeason: October to March (calmest seas, best visibility)
highlights: Coral garden snorkeling in protected marine park waters
Green and hawksbill sea turtle encounters
Colourful reef fish including parrotfish and butterflyfish
Glass-bottom boat ride to the reef
Lunch on a sandbar between snorkel sessions
notes: Park entry fee of $12 (non-resident) applies on top of boat/guide costs. Snorkel gear is usually provided. The best visibility is during the northeast monsoon (Oct-Mar); during the southeast monsoon (Apr-Sep) seas can be rough and some operators pause trips.

name: Snorkeling Kisite-Mpunguti
description: Journey to Kenya's southernmost marine park for what many consider the country's finest snorkeling. Kisite-Mpunguti Marine Park protects pristine coral reefs and a resident pod of bottlenose dolphins. The boat ride from Shimoni village passes mangrove-fringed channels and small islands before reaching gin-clear waters alive with manta rays, whale sharks (seasonal), and hundreds of reef fish species.
shortDescription: Kenya's premier snorkeling destination . dolphins, pristine reefs, and crystal-clear waters at Kisite-Mpunguti.
bestSeason: October to March (calm seas, best visibility)
highlights: Resident pod of Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins
Some of Kenya's healthiest and most colourful coral reefs
Seasonal whale shark and manta ray sightings
Seafood lunch on Wasini Island included in most packages
Scenic dhow boat ride through mangrove channels
notes: Trips depart from Shimoni, about 1.5 hours south of Diani Beach. Most packages include transport from Diani, boat trip, snorkel gear, park fees, and lunch on Wasini Island. Not operational during heavy southeast monsoon (roughly June-September).

name: PADI Open Water Course
description: Earn your PADI Open Water certification in the warm, clear waters of Kenya's Indian Ocean coast. Over three to four days, you'll progress from pool skills to open-water dives on coral reefs, completing four ocean dives that qualify you to dive independently to 18 metres worldwide. Kenya's year-round warm water (26-30 °C) makes it one of the most comfortable places on Earth to learn.
shortDescription: Earn your PADI Open Water diving certification on Kenya's warm coral reefs over 3-4 days.
bestSeason: November to April (best visibility, calmest seas)
highlights: Internationally recognised PADI certification valid worldwide
Warm water (26-30 °C) . no wetsuit stress
Coral reef dives with tropical fish, turtles, and rays
Small class sizes (max 4 students per instructor)
E-learning option to complete theory before arrival
notes: Minimum age 10 years (Junior Open Water) or 15 years for full certification. A medical self-declaration is required; certain conditions need physician clearance. Allow 24 hours after your last dive before flying. All equipment is provided.

name: PADI Discover Scuba Diving
description: Try scuba diving without committing to a full course on a PADI Discover Scuba Diving experience. After a short pool briefing, you'll descend onto a shallow coral reef with an instructor by your side at all times. It is the perfect introduction for anyone curious about the underwater world . no prior experience needed, just a sense of adventure.
shortDescription: Try scuba diving for the first time with an instructor on a shallow coral reef . no experience needed.
highlights: No certification or experience required
One-on-one instructor supervision throughout
Shallow reef dive (max 12m depth)
Encounter tropical fish, sea stars, and corals
Credits toward full Open Water course if you continue
notes: Minimum age 10 years. Participants must be comfortable in water but do not need to be strong swimmers. Medical questionnaire required. The experience does not certify you . it is an introductory taste. Allow 24 hours before flying after diving.

name: Deep-Sea Fishing Watamu
description: Watamu is East Africa's premier deep-sea fishing destination, with productive offshore waters that have yielded multiple world records for marlin, sailfish, and yellowfin tuna. Charter a fully equipped sport-fishing boat and head to the continental shelf drop-off, just 15-20 nautical miles offshore, where the big pelagics patrol the deep blue.
shortDescription: World-class deep-sea fishing off Watamu . marlin, sailfish, and tuna on the continental shelf.
highlights: World-record fishing grounds for marlin and sailfish
Short run (15-20 nm) to the continental shelf drop-off
Tag-and-release ethos for billfish conservation
Full equipment and experienced crew included
Combine with snorkeling or beach time for a full day
notes: Boats range from 25-foot open boats (budget) to 45-foot sportfishers (luxury). Tag-and-release is standard for billfish. Prices are per boat, not per person . most accommodate 4-6 anglers. Bring sunscreen, hat, and polarised sunglasses.

name: Deep-Sea Fishing Diani
description: Head offshore from Diani Beach aboard a chartered sport-fishing vessel to target sailfish, marlin, wahoo, dorado, and kingfish in the deep Pemba Channel. Diani's proximity to the Shimoni deep-water channel makes for productive fishing year-round, with experienced skippers who know every ledge and current.
shortDescription: Offshore sport fishing from Diani Beach . sailfish, marlin, and wahoo in the Pemba Channel.
highlights: Access to the productive Pemba Channel fishing grounds
Half-day and full-day charter options
Wahoo, dorado, tuna, and billfish depending on season
All tackle, bait, and crew included
Easy transfers from Diani Beach hotels
notes: Half-day trips (5 hours) focus on reef and mid-water species; full-day trips (9 hours) reach the deep channel for billfish. Price is per boat. Book at least a day in advance during high season (Dec-Jan). Bring seasickness medication if prone.

name: Whale Shark Encounter
description: Swim alongside the world's largest fish . the gentle whale shark . in the warm waters off Kenya's coast. These magnificent creatures, reaching up to 12 metres in length, visit Kenya's coastal waters seasonally to feed on plankton blooms. Guided snorkel encounters are conducted ethically with strict approach protocols to minimise disturbance to these endangered animals.
shortDescription: Snorkel alongside gentle whale sharks off Kenya's coast during the seasonal plankton migration.
highlights: Swim with the world's largest fish (up to 12m long)
Ethical encounters following international best-practice protocols
Seasonal event . a genuine bucket-list experience
Marine biologist briefing before each encounter
Underwater photography opportunities
notes: Sightings are not guaranteed as whale sharks are wild animals; success rates are highest in January-February. Strong swimming ability required. No touching or riding the animals. Operators use spotter boats and sometimes light aircraft to locate sharks. Minimum age typically 10-12 years.

name: Dolphin Watching
description: Board a traditional dhow or motorboat and cruise to dolphin hotspots along the Kenya coast. Resident pods of Indo-Pacific bottlenose and spinner dolphins are regularly encountered, often approaching boats with playful curiosity. Many trips offer the chance to slip into the water and snorkel alongside the dolphins in their natural habitat.
shortDescription: Boat trip to encounter resident dolphin pods along Kenya's coast, with optional in-water snorkeling.
highlights: Bottlenose and spinner dolphin encounters
Optional in-water snorkeling with dolphins
Traditional dhow sailing experience
Often combined with Kisite-Mpunguti reef snorkeling
Seafood lunch on Wasini Island
notes: Most dolphin trips are combined with Kisite-Mpunguti snorkeling and Wasini Island lunch. Dolphin sighting rates are high (80%+) but not guaranteed. Ethical operators maintain safe distances and do not chase pods. Trips are weather-dependent . seas can be rough June-September.

name: Glass-Bottom Boat Tour
description: See the colourful underwater world without getting wet aboard a glass-bottom boat gliding over Kenya's coral reefs. Perfect for non-swimmers and families with young children, these boats feature transparent viewing panels that reveal parrotfish, starfish, sea urchins, and coral formations in vivid detail just a metre below the hull.
shortDescription: View coral reefs and tropical fish through a glass-bottom boat . perfect for non-swimmers and families.
highlights: No swimming or snorkeling required . view from the boat
Suitable for all ages including small children
Colourful coral gardens and tropical reef fish
Marine park entry fee often included
Combine with a beach picnic on a sandbar
notes: Marine park fees ($12-15 per non-resident adult) may be extra depending on the operator. Best at high tide when water is deeper over the reefs. Shorter trips (1.5 hrs) are available in Diani; longer tours (4 hrs) often include snorkeling stops.

name: Dhow Sunset Cruise Lamu
description: Sail into the golden Indian Ocean sunset aboard a traditional Lamu dhow, handcrafted from mangrove wood using centuries-old techniques. As the sky shifts from amber to deep violet, sip sundowner drinks and watch the ancient stone waterfront of Lamu Town glow in the fading light . a scene virtually unchanged since the 14th century.
shortDescription: Traditional dhow sunset sail through Lamu's ancient waterfront . sundowners on the Indian Ocean.
highlights: Traditional handcrafted mangrove-wood dhow sailing
Stunning Indian Ocean sunset views
Views of Lamu's UNESCO World Heritage waterfront
Sundowner drinks and snacks on board
Intimate experience with small group (2-8 guests)
notes: Dhows are wind-powered with no engine . departure times depend on tides and wind conditions. Some operators add a small motor for reliability. Life jackets are provided but facilities are basic. Bring a light layer as ocean breezes can be cool after sunset.

name: Dhow Full-Day Trip Lamu
description: Spend an entire day sailing the Lamu Archipelago aboard a traditional dhow, visiting deserted sandbanks, snorkeling over coral reefs, and feasting on freshly grilled seafood prepared by your dhow crew on a private beach. The route typically includes Manda Island, Shela Beach, and hidden mangrove channels teeming with birdlife.
shortDescription: Full-day dhow sailing adventure around Lamu's islands with snorkeling, sandbanks, and fresh seafood.
highlights: Island-hopping through the Lamu Archipelago
Snorkeling over pristine coral reefs
Freshly grilled seafood lunch on a deserted sandbank
Mangrove channel cruising and birdwatching
Manda Island and Shela Beach exploration
notes: Price usually includes crew, snorkel gear, and seafood lunch. Bring sunscreen, hat, towel, and waterproof bag for electronics. Trips are weather-dependent . rough seas during the Kaskazi or Kusi monsoons may limit sailing routes.

name: Multi-Day Dhow Safari
description: Embark on a multi-day dhow expedition through the remote reaches of the Lamu Archipelago, sleeping on deserted islands under the stars and exploring uninhabited coastline that few travellers ever reach. These safaris follow the ancient trading routes of Swahili sailors, combining snorkeling, fishing, beachcombing, and island exploration into a true maritime adventure.
shortDescription: Multi-day sailing expedition through the remote Lamu Archipelago . island camping, snorkeling, and Swahili culture.
highlights: Sleep on deserted islands under the Milky Way
Snorkel pristine reefs far from tourist areas
Fresh seafood cooked on the beach by expert dhow crew
Follow ancient Swahili trading routes
Complete digital detox . no signal, no distractions
notes: Pack light . space on traditional dhows is limited. Sleeping is on deck or on the beach on mattresses provided by the crew. Toilet facilities are basic (bush or sea). Not recommended for those who require comfort. Best booked October-March when seas are calmest.

name: Kitesurfing Lesson
description: Harness the power of the Indian Ocean trade winds on a kitesurfing lesson at one of Kenya's premier kite beaches. Diani and Che Shale offer wide, flat lagoons with consistent side-onshore winds . ideal learning conditions. Professional IKO-certified instructors guide you from kite control on the beach through body-dragging to your first rides on the board.
shortDescription: Learn to kitesurf on Kenya's wind-blessed coast with IKO-certified instructors in ideal lagoon conditions.
bestSeason: June to October (strongest, most consistent trade winds)
highlights: IKO-certified instruction with professional equipment
Flat, waist-deep lagoons for safe learning
Consistent trade winds (Jun-Oct and Dec-Mar)
One-on-one or small group instruction
Stunning beach setting with warm water
notes: No prior experience needed. Minimum age typically 12 years, minimum weight 40 kg. The best wind season is June-October (Kusi monsoon). A secondary wind season runs December-March (Kaskazi). Lessons include all equipment. Expect to need 6-12 hours of instruction before riding independently.

name: Kitesurfing 3-Day Course
description: Commit to a three-day kitesurfing course and progress from complete beginner to riding independently. Over nine hours of structured instruction, you'll master kite theory, safety systems, body-dragging, water relaunching, and board riding. By day three, most students are cruising across the lagoon with the wind in their hair and a grin on their face.
shortDescription: Three-day structured kitesurfing course . from zero to riding independently in Kenya's perfect lagoon conditions.
highlights: Complete progression from beginner to independent riding
9 hours of professional IKO-certified instruction
All equipment included (kite, board, harness, wetsuit if needed)
Theory, safety, body-dragging, and board starts covered
IKO certification card upon completion
notes: Three consecutive days recommended but can be spread over a week if wind conditions require. Physical fitness helps . kitesurfing uses core and upper body. No prior experience needed. Most schools offer package discounts for the 3-day course vs. individual lessons.

name: Stand-Up Paddleboarding
description: Glide across Kenya's turquoise coastal waters on a stand-up paddleboard (SUP), one of the easiest and most relaxing water sports to pick up. Paddle over shallow reefs spotting fish below, explore mangrove creeks, or simply cruise along the beach at sunset. SUP is suitable for all ages and fitness levels.
shortDescription: Relaxed stand-up paddleboarding over turquoise waters . spot fish, explore creeks, or cruise at sunset.
highlights: Easy to learn . most people stand up within minutes
See reef fish and marine life beneath the board
Explore mangrove channels and hidden coves
Great core workout disguised as fun
Sunset SUP sessions available
notes: Boards and paddles are provided. Life jackets available on request. Calm mornings and evenings offer the flattest water. Reef shoes recommended. No experience necessary . a brief orientation is given before each rental.

name: Jet Ski Experience
description: Feel the rush of adrenaline as you throttle across the Indian Ocean on a high-powered jet ski. Speed along the coast with the spray in your face, perform sweeping turns in open water, and take in the palm-fringed shoreline from a thrilling new perspective. Sessions range from quick 15-minute blasts to extended 30-minute cruises.
shortDescription: High-speed jet ski ride along Kenya's coast . pure adrenaline on the Indian Ocean.
highlights: High-speed thrills on modern jet skis
Scenic coastal views from the water
No experience or licence required
Brief safety orientation before riding
15-minute or 30-minute session options
notes: Minimum age is typically 16 to ride solo; younger riders can go as passengers with an adult. Life jacket mandatory and provided. Riders are briefed on safety zones and must stay within designated areas to protect marine park zones. Price varies by duration and operator.

name: Kayaking
region: Diani Beach, Watamu, Lamu, Lake Naivasha
description: Paddle a sit-on-top kayak through crystal-clear coastal waters, up mangrove-lined creeks, or across the freshwater expanse of Lake Naivasha surrounded by hippos and pelicans. Kayaking offers a quiet, self-paced way to explore Kenya's diverse waterways . from reef-protected lagoons to birdlife-rich lake shores.
shortDescription: Kayak through coastal lagoons, mangrove creeks, or Lake Naivasha . a quiet way to explore Kenya's waterways.
highlights: Explore mangrove channels and hidden coves
Spot marine life through clear water beneath the kayak
Lake Naivasha kayaking with hippo and pelican sightings
Single and tandem kayaks available
Perfect sunrise or sunset activity
notes: Sit-on-top kayaks are stable and easy for beginners. Life jackets provided. On Lake Naivasha, maintain a safe distance from hippos . a guide is recommended. Coastal kayaking is best at high tide. Bring waterproof sun protection.

name: Tandem Skydiving Diani
description: Leap from an aircraft at 10,000-12,000 feet and freefall over the stunning Diani coastline before your parachute opens to reveal a breathtaking panorama of white sand, turquoise ocean, and lush coastal forest. Strapped to a certified tandem instructor, no experience is needed . just courage and a desire for the ultimate thrill.
shortDescription: Tandem skydive over Diani Beach . freefall from 10,000+ feet with Indian Ocean views.
highlights: Freefall at 200 km/h for 30-45 seconds
Parachute descent with panoramic coastal views
Professional tandem instructor . no experience needed
GoPro video and photos available for purchase
Certificate of completion
notes: Minimum age 16 (18 to jump without parental consent). Maximum weight typically 100 kg. Not recommended for pregnant women or those with heart conditions. Jumps are weather-dependent . wind, cloud, and rain may cause rescheduling. Book at least a day in advance.

name: Banana Boat Ride
description: Hold on tight as a speedboat tows an inflatable banana boat at high speed across the ocean, bouncing over waves and sending riders tumbling into the warm Indian Ocean with shrieks of laughter. A favourite for groups and families, the banana boat ride is pure, uncomplicated fun and one of the coast's most popular beach activities.
shortDescription: High-speed inflatable banana boat ride . bouncing waves, splashing fun, and guaranteed laughs.
highlights: Fast-paced, laugh-out-loud group fun on the water
Suitable for children and adults alike
No experience or skill required
Life jackets provided for safety
Combine with other beach water sports
notes: Price is per ride (not per person) . boats accommodate 4-8 riders. Life jackets are mandatory and provided. Riders will likely fall off . wear swimwear and secure sunglasses/hats. Not recommended for those with back or neck problems. Available at most major beach resorts.

name: Mt. Kenya Trek (Budget)
description: Summit Africa's second-highest mountain on a budget trek to Point Lenana (4,985m), the highest non-technical peak. The Sirimon or Chogoria route takes you through bamboo forest, giant heather moorland, and surreal Afro-alpine landscapes of giant lobelias and groundsel before a pre-dawn summit push rewarded by sunrise views stretching to Kilimanjaro and the Indian Ocean.
shortDescription: Budget trek to Point Lenana (4,985m) on Mt Kenya . bamboo forests, Afro-alpine landscapes, and stunning summit views.
operators: Mt Kenya Guides & Porters Safari Club
highlights: Summit Point Lenana at 4,985m . Africa's second-highest mountain
Surreal Afro-alpine zone with giant lobelias and groundsel
Pre-dawn summit push with sunrise over the African plains
Diverse vegetation zones from rainforest to glacial valleys
UNESCO World Heritage Site and Biosphere Reserve
notes: Altitude sickness is a real risk . acclimatise properly with a 4-5 day itinerary rather than rushing in 3 days. Budget treks use basic mountain huts (bandas) and include guide, porter, park fees, and meals. Bring warm layers . temperatures drop to -10 °C near the summit. Minimum recommended fitness: ability to hike 6-8 hours daily.

name: Mt. Kenya Trek (Luxury)
description: Experience Mount Kenya's majesty in comfort on a luxury guided trek featuring premium tented camps, gourmet bush cuisine, and comprehensive porter support. The 5-6 day itinerary follows scenic routes with proper acclimatisation, allowing you to savour the journey through cloud forest, moorland, and Afro-alpine zones before summiting Point Lenana at dawn.
shortDescription: Luxury Mt Kenya trek with premium camps, gourmet cuisine, and full porter support to Point Lenana.
highlights: Premium tented camps with hot showers and mess tents
Gourmet meals prepared by expedition chefs
Comprehensive porter and guide team (1:1 ratio)
Proper 5-6 day acclimatisation schedule
Combine with Laikipia safari for a complete experience
notes: Luxury treks include all park fees, equipment (except personal clothing), meals, and transfers from Nairobi. Some operators add a pre-trek night at a luxury lodge on the mountain slopes. The Chogoria-Sirimon traverse is the most scenic route option.

name: Mt. Longonot Hike
region: Mt Longonot National Park, Nakuru County
description: Hike up the steep flanks of Mt Longonot, a dormant stratovolcano rising from the floor of the Great Rift Valley. The trail ascends through scrubby bushland to the crater rim, where a circumnavigation path offers 360-degree views of Lake Naivasha, the Rift Valley escarpment, and the forested crater floor far below. It is one of the best day hikes near Nairobi.
shortDescription: Hike a dormant volcano in the Rift Valley with panoramic crater-rim views of Lake Naivasha.
highlights: Dramatic volcanic crater rim walk
Panoramic views of Lake Naivasha and the Rift Valley
Spot buffalo and giraffe on the crater floor (from above)
Just 90 minutes from Nairobi . perfect day trip
Excellent cardiovascular workout with 1,000m elevation gain
notes: The ascent is steep and exposed . start early (before 8am) to avoid midday heat. Carry at least 2 litres of water per person. The crater rim circuit adds 2-3 hours. KWS park entry fee is $26 for non-residents. A ranger guide is available for a small fee.

name: Mt. Suswa Exploration
description: Explore the otherworldly landscapes of Mt Suswa, a shield volcano featuring a collapsed outer crater, an inner crater with a forested 'island', and an extensive network of lava tube caves once used as Maasai shelters. The hike combines geological wonder with cultural discovery . Maasai guides share legends of the caves and the mountain's spiritual significance.
shortDescription: Explore a shield volcano with lava tube caves and a Maasai-guided geological adventure.
highlights: Extensive lava tube cave system to explore
Double crater . outer and inner . with forested 'island'
Maasai guide sharing cultural legends and history
Baboon colonies in the caves and crater rim
Dramatic, uncrowded volcanic landscape
notes: A 4x4 vehicle is required to reach the trailhead due to rough access roads. Bring a torch/headlamp for the lava tube caves. A Maasai community fee ($10-15) is payable at the gate. The mountain is approximately 2 hours from Nairobi. Not well-signposted . a local guide is essential.

name: Ngong Hills Walk
description: Walk the iconic Ngong Hills, the undulating ridge on Nairobi's southwestern doorstep immortalised by Karen Blixen in 'Out of Africa'. The trail traverses seven rounded peaks with views across the Great Rift Valley to one side and Nairobi's skyline to the other . a remarkable juxtaposition of wilderness and cityscape that captures Kenya's dual character.
shortDescription: Walk the 'Out of Africa' hills on Nairobi's doorstep with Rift Valley and city skyline views.
highlights: Seven peaks with panoramic Rift Valley views
Nairobi skyline visible to the east on clear days
Karen Blixen 'Out of Africa' literary connection
KWS ranger escort included for security
Easy access . just 30 minutes from Nairobi CBD
notes: KWS rangers accompany all hikers for security (mandatory, small fee). The trail is exposed . bring sunscreen, hat, and water. Start early to avoid afternoon cloud cover. The walk can be done as a one-way traverse with vehicle pickup at the far end, or an out-and-back.

name: Hell's Gate Cycling
region: Hell's Gate National Park, Nakuru County
description: Cycle through one of the few Kenyan national parks where you can walk and ride among wildlife without a vehicle. Hell's Gate's dramatic volcanic cliffs, towering rock formations, and geothermal steam vents create an almost cinematic landscape . it was, in fact, the inspiration for the setting of Disney's 'The Lion King'. Bike past zebra, giraffe, and buffalo on your way to the narrow Fischer's Tower gorge.
shortDescription: Cycle through dramatic volcanic cliffs alongside zebra and giraffe in Hell's Gate . the 'Lion King' landscape.
highlights: Cycle alongside wildlife . zebra, giraffe, buffalo, and eland
Dramatic volcanic cliffs and Fischer's Tower rock pillar
Hell's Gate Gorge walk with natural hot springs
Inspiration for Disney's 'The Lion King' landscape
One of the few parks allowing cycling and walking
notes: Bike rental ($5-10) is available at the Elsa Gate entrance. Park entry fee is $26 for non-residents. The gorge walk requires an additional guide fee. Flash floods can occur in the gorge during heavy rains . check conditions. Combine with Lake Naivasha for a full day trip. Bring plenty of water . the park is hot and dry.

name: White Water Rafting Sagana
description: Tackle Class II-IV rapids on the Tana River near Sagana, Kenya's white-water capital. Expert raft guides navigate your crew through churning rapids named 'Cascade', 'The Cheese Grater', and 'Jungle Run' as the river cuts through lush riverine forest. Between rapids, float through calm pools and enjoy the tropical bird chorus overhead.
shortDescription: White-water rafting on the Tana River . Class II-IV rapids through lush forest near Sagana.
bestSeason: Year-round (best after rainy seasons for higher water)
highlights: Class II-IV rapids with exciting names
Professional guides and all safety equipment provided
Lush riverine forest setting
Perfect team-building activity
Just 2 hours from Nairobi
notes: Minimum age is typically 12-14 years depending on water levels and operator. Non-swimmers are accepted with life jackets. The river is dam-controlled . water levels can change. Wear shoes that can get wet (no flip-flops). Bring a change of dry clothes.

name: Bungee Jumping
description: Take the leap from a purpose-built platform high above the Tana River on one of East Africa's few bungee jumping sites. The heart-stopping freefall sends you plummeting toward the river below before the cord catches and bounces you back skyward. It is an intense adrenaline rush that lasts just seconds but creates memories for a lifetime.
shortDescription: Bungee jump from a platform above the Tana River . a heart-stopping freefall near Sagana.
highlights: Heart-stopping freefall above the Tana River
Professional equipment inspected to international standards
Photo and video packages available
Certificate of bravery upon completion
Combine with white-water rafting for a full adventure day
notes: Minimum age 14 years. Maximum weight typically 120 kg. Not recommended for those with heart conditions, back problems, or pregnancy. The entire experience takes about 30 minutes including harness fitting and safety briefing. Often combined with rafting as a half-day adventure package.

name: Zip-Lining Kereita
description: Soar through the canopy of Kereita Forest on a series of zip-lines connecting platforms high in the indigenous trees. The course features multiple lines of varying lengths and heights, offering aerial views of the forest floor below and the surrounding Aberdare foothills. It is one of the most accessible adventure activities near Nairobi.
shortDescription: Zip-line through indigenous forest canopy near Nairobi at Kereita Forest adventure park.
highlights: Multiple zip-lines through indigenous forest canopy
Suitable for children and adults
Professional safety equipment and guides
Beautiful forest setting just 1 hour from Nairobi
Combine with hiking, mountain biking, or horse riding in the forest
notes: Minimum age varies by line . some are suitable for children as young as 5 with parental consent. Closed-toe shoes required. Long hair must be tied back. The forest also offers hiking trails, mountain biking, and horse riding. Entry to the forest is approximately $4.

name: Quad Biking
description: Tear across off-road trails on a powerful quad bike (ATV), kicking up dust on savanna tracks, splashing through forest puddles, or cruising along coastal backroads. Quad biking is available at several locations across Kenya, from beachside Diani to the volcanic landscapes around Lake Naivasha and forested areas on Nairobi's outskirts.
shortDescription: Off-road quad biking adventure through savanna, forest, or coastal trails across Kenya.
highlights: Guided off-road trails through diverse terrain
Automatic quad bikes . no experience needed
Scenic routes through bush, forest, or coastal paths
Brief training session before each ride
Available for individuals, couples, or groups
notes: Minimum age is typically 12-16 for solo riders; younger children can ride as passengers with an adult on larger quads. Helmets provided and mandatory. Long trousers and closed-toe shoes recommended. Goggles or sunglasses protect against dust.

name: Hot Air Balloon Safari Mara
description: Rise with the sun in a hot air balloon and drift silently over the endless golden plains of the Maasai Mara as the African bush awakens below. From altitude, watch herds of wildebeest, zebra, and elephant moving across the landscape, spot hippos wallowing in the Mara River, and . if timing is right . witness the Great Migration from the most spectacular vantage point imaginable. The flight concludes with a champagne bush breakfast on the savanna.
shortDescription: Sunrise balloon flight over the Maasai Mara followed by champagne bush breakfast on the savanna.
highlights: Sunrise flight over the Maasai Mara plains
Bird's-eye view of wildlife herds and river crossings
Champagne bush breakfast after landing
Flight certificate signed by the pilot
Opportunity to watch balloon inflation . a spectacle in itself
notes: Flights depart before dawn (pickup from camp around 5-5:30am). Flight duration is approximately 1 hour depending on wind. Children under 7 are generally not permitted. Maximum weight restrictions may apply. Flights may be cancelled due to wind . a backup date or full refund is standard. Book well in advance during peak season.

name: Helicopter Scenic Flight
region: Nairobi, Maasai Mara, Mt Kenya, Rift Valley
description: See Kenya's most dramatic landscapes from the cockpit of a private helicopter on a scenic flight over the Great Rift Valley, Lake Nakuru, Mount Kenya, or the Maasai Mara. Helicopters offer the flexibility to hover over points of interest, land on remote hilltops for sundowners, and access terrain that fixed-wing aircraft cannot reach.
shortDescription: Private helicopter scenic flight over the Rift Valley, lakes, mountains, or the Maasai Mara.
highlights: Low-level flying over wildlife herds (where permitted)
Land on remote hilltops for sundowner drinks
Door-off options for unobstructed photography
Customisable routes . you choose the destination
Experienced bush pilots with thousands of hours
notes: Prices are per hour for the helicopter (typically seats 4-6), not per person . split among passengers for better value. Door-off flying is available for photography but requires safety harnesses. Route flexibility is subject to airspace restrictions. Charter from Wilson Airport, Nairobi.

name: Full-Day Helicopter Safari
description: Experience a full day of aerial adventure on a private helicopter safari that combines flying with ground-based experiences. A typical itinerary might include a morning flight over the Rift Valley escarpment, a bush landing for a guided nature walk, lunch at a remote lodge, an afternoon flying low over Lake Naivasha or the Mara, and a sundowner landing on a scenic ridge.
shortDescription: Full-day private helicopter safari combining aerial sightseeing with bush landings, walks, and exclusive dining.
highlights: Multiple scenic landings in remote locations
Bush walk, picnic lunch, and sundowner included
Cover vast distances in a single day
Fully customisable itinerary based on interests
Private and exclusive . just your group
notes: Price includes helicopter charter, fuel, pilot, and landing fees. Ground activities (lunch, walks, entry fees) may be additional depending on the package. Suitable for 2-5 passengers depending on helicopter type. Book at least a week in advance for bespoke itineraries.

name: Multi-Day Helicopter Safari
description: The ultimate way to experience Kenya: a multi-day helicopter safari that leapfrogs between the country's most remote and spectacular locations. Over five to six days, fly from the northern deserts of Turkana to the forests of Mt Kenya, the flamingo lakes of the Rift Valley, the Maasai Mara's migration, and the coral coast of Lamu . staying at exclusive lodges along the way.
shortDescription: Ultimate multi-day helicopter expedition across Kenya's most remote and spectacular landscapes.
highlights: Cover multiple ecosystems from desert to coast in days
Land in locations no road can reach
Stay at Kenya's most exclusive and remote lodges
Fully bespoke itinerary designed around your interests
Experienced expedition pilot who doubles as a guide
notes: These safaris are fully bespoke . no two itineraries are alike. Pricing varies significantly based on routing, accommodation choices, and group size. Lead time of 2-3 months recommended. Luggage weight limits apply for helicopters (typically 15 kg soft bag). Travel insurance with helicopter evacuation cover is essential.

name: Horseback Safari (Short Ride)
description: Ride through the African bush on horseback for a two-hour encounter with wildlife that no vehicle safari can match. Horses allow you to approach plains game much more closely than a Land Cruiser . zebra and giraffe are often unbothered by riders, creating extraordinary close encounters in a uniquely silent, immersive setting.
shortDescription: Two-hour horseback ride through the bush alongside zebra, giraffe, and antelope.
highlights: Ride alongside wildlife . zebra, giraffe, antelope
Quiet, immersive experience impossible from a vehicle
Well-schooled horses suited to the African bush
Expert riding guides with bush knowledge
Scenic landscapes of Laikipia or Mara conservancies
notes: Intermediate riding ability is usually required (ability to walk, trot, and canter confidently). Weight limits apply (typically 90-95 kg). Riders are matched to suitable horses. Hard hats provided. Long trousers and closed-toe shoes/boots required.

name: Multi-Day Horseback Safari
description: Embark on a multi-day riding adventure across Kenya's vast wilderness, covering 20-40 km per day on horseback through landscapes teeming with wildlife. By day, ride across open plains, through river crossings, and along forested ridges. By night, camp under the stars at mobile fly-camps or stay at exclusive riding lodges. This is the quintessential African horseback safari.
shortDescription: Multi-day riding expedition across Kenya's wilderness . 20-40 km daily through Big Five country.
highlights: Ride 20-40 km per day through Big Five territory
Mobile fly-camps or exclusive bush lodges each night
River crossings, open plains, and forested ridges
Experienced back-up team manages camp logistics
Sundowners and bush dinners under the stars
notes: Strong intermediate to advanced riding ability is essential . riders must be confident at all paces across open terrain. Fitness is important as you will spend 4-6 hours in the saddle daily. Weight limit typically 90 kg. Minimum age 16. All-inclusive pricing covers accommodation, meals, horses, guides, and conservancy fees.

name: Camel Trek Laikipia
description: Trek through Kenya's wild northern frontier on camelback, following routes used by Samburu pastoralists for centuries. Camels carry your supplies while you walk or ride through sun-baked landscapes of ochre plains, acacia woodland, and dramatic escarpments. Evenings are spent at mobile fly-camps with traditional Samburu campfire stories under vast starlit skies.
shortDescription: Camelback trek through northern Kenya's wild frontier with Samburu guides and fly-camp accommodation.
highlights: Authentic Samburu-led camel caravans
Walk or ride through stunning semi-arid landscapes
Mobile fly-camp accommodation with bush showers
Star-gazing far from any light pollution
Cultural exchange with Samburu warriors and elders
notes: No riding experience needed . camels are gentle and well-trained. Walking is also an option while camels carry luggage. A reasonable level of fitness is required for walking days (10-15 km). Camps are comfortable but basic . expect bucket showers and pit latrines. Daytime temperatures can exceed 35 °C . sun protection essential.

name: Camel Day Walk
description: Experience a taste of northern Kenya's camel culture on a guided day walk with camels carrying your picnic supplies. Walk alongside Samburu guides through bush country, learning about traditional navigation, animal tracking, and plant identification, before settling under an acacia tree for a bush lunch prepared by your camel team.
shortDescription: Guided day walk with Samburu camel team through the bush, culminating in a bush picnic lunch.
highlights: Walk through the bush with a camel caravan
Samburu guide sharing traditional knowledge
Bush picnic lunch under acacia shade
Wildlife sightings en route . giraffe, antelope, birds
Gentle introduction to camel safari life
notes: No riding ability needed . walking is the primary mode with camels carrying supplies. Suitable for older children (8+) and moderately fit adults. Wear comfortable walking shoes, sun protection, and bring binoculars. Walks typically cover 8-12 km depending on the group.

name: Bomas of Kenya
description: Visit Bomas of Kenya, a living cultural centre showcasing the traditional homesteads, music, and dance of Kenya's 42+ ethnic communities. The highlight is a vibrant afternoon performance featuring Maasai jumping dances, Kamba acrobatics, Luo Ohangla rhythms, and Kikuyu ceremonial songs . all performed by a professional troupe in an open-air auditorium.
shortDescription: Living cultural centre showcasing traditional music, dance, and homesteads of Kenya's 42+ ethnic communities.
highlights: Live traditional dance and music performances daily
Replica homesteads of Kenya's major ethnic communities
Interactive audience participation in dances
Artisan craft shopping at the cultural village
Just 10 km from Nairobi CBD near the national park
notes: Afternoon performances are typically at 2:30pm on weekdays, 3:30pm on weekends and holidays . check times in advance. Photography is permitted during performances. Located adjacent to Nairobi National Park . easily combined. Allow 2.5-3 hours for a thorough visit.

name: Karen Blixen Museum
description: Step into the world of 'Out of Africa' at the Karen Blixen Museum, the preserved farmhouse where the Danish author lived from 1917 to 1931. The colonial-era building houses original furniture, photographs, and personal effects that bring Blixen's Kenya to life. The manicured gardens offer views of the Ngong Hills that she immortalised in her memoir.
shortDescription: Tour the preserved farmhouse of 'Out of Africa' author Karen Blixen, with Ngong Hills views.
highlights: Original Karen Blixen farmhouse with period furnishings
Views of the Ngong Hills from the garden
Personal photographs and 'Out of Africa' memorabilia
Guided tours available with knowledgeable docents
Beautiful grounds perfect for a quiet afternoon stroll
notes: Open daily 8:30am-6:00pm. Guided tours are available and recommended to bring the history alive. Located in Karen suburb, 20 minutes from Nairobi CBD. Easily combined with Giraffe Centre and Kazuri Beads, both nearby.

name: Nairobi National Museum
description: Explore Kenya's natural and cultural heritage under one roof at the Nairobi National Museum, home to a comprehensive collection spanning paleontology, ethnography, contemporary art, and natural history. Star exhibits include a cast of 'Turkana Boy' (the most complete early human skeleton ever found), an extensive bird collection, and the Joy Adamson gallery of Kenya's tribal peoples.
shortDescription: Kenya's premier museum . paleontology, ethnography, art, and natural history in central Nairobi.
highlights: Turkana Boy and early human fossil exhibits
Joy Adamson ethnographic painting collection
Snake park and botanical garden on the grounds
Contemporary Kenyan art galleries
Central location on Museum Hill . easy to reach
notes: Open daily 8:30am-5:30pm. Combined tickets with the Snake Park and Botanical Garden available. The on-site gift shop sells quality Kenyan crafts. Allow 2-3 hours for a thorough visit. Audio guides available in multiple languages.

name: Fort Jesus Mombasa
description: Explore Fort Jesus, the imposing 16th-century Portuguese fortress that guards the entrance to Mombasa's old harbour. Built in 1593 to secure Portugal's trade route to India, the fort has been attacked, captured, and rebuilt by Portuguese, Omani Arab, and British forces over four centuries. Now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, its coral-stone walls house a museum of coastal archaeology and Swahili maritime history.
shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Portuguese fortress in Mombasa . 400 years of coastal history and Swahili culture.
highlights: UNESCO World Heritage Site dating to 1593
Coral-stone fortress architecture and ramparts
Museum of Swahili culture and maritime archaeology
Harbour views from the battlements
Combine with a walking tour of Mombasa Old Town
notes: Open daily 8:00am-6:00pm. Guided tours are available and recommended. The fort is best visited in the morning before the heat of the day. Located at the edge of Mombasa Old Town . combine with a walking tour of the narrow streets and spice markets.

name: Lamu Museums Package
description: Visit the interconnected museums of Lamu Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the oldest continually inhabited Swahili settlement in East Africa. The package typically includes the Lamu Museum (Swahili culture and dhow-building), the Swahili House Museum (restored 18th-century merchant's home), and the Lamu Fort (built by the Sultan of Oman in 1821).
shortDescription: Museum circuit through Lamu's UNESCO Old Town . Swahili culture, dhow heritage, and Omani fort.
highlights: UNESCO World Heritage Swahili settlement
Lamu Museum with dhow-building exhibits and navigation tools
Swahili House Museum . restored 18th-century merchant's home
Lamu Fort . 19th-century Omani fortification
Walking through car-free streets unchanged for centuries
notes: Lamu is car-free . all movement is on foot or by donkey. The museums are within walking distance of each other in the Old Town. A local guide is recommended for context and to navigate the labyrinthine streets. Best visited in the morning when it is cooler. Dress modestly as Lamu is a predominantly Muslim community.

name: Gede Ruins
description: Wander through the atmospheric ruins of Gede, a mysterious 12th-century Swahili trading town abandoned in the 17th century and swallowed by coastal forest. The coral-stone remains of mosques, palaces, and merchants' houses rise from a canopy of baobab and buttress-rooted trees, creating an eerie, enchanting atmosphere. Gede is one of the most evocative archaeological sites on the East African coast.
shortDescription: Atmospheric 12th-century Swahili ruins hidden in coastal forest near Watamu . mosques, palaces, and mystery.
highlights: Coral-stone mosque, palace, and merchant house ruins
Ancient baobab trees growing through the structures
Small on-site museum with excavated artefacts
Golden-rumped elephant shrew sightings in the forest
Atmospheric forest setting . a photographer's dream
notes: A guide is available at the entrance and recommended to bring the ruins to life. The site is about 15 minutes from Watamu and easily combined with a beach day. Wear comfortable shoes . paths are uneven. The adjacent Kipepeo Butterfly House is worth a visit.

name: Maasai Village Visit
description: Step inside a traditional Maasai manyatta (homestead) for a guided cultural experience led by Maasai warriors and elders. Learn about their semi-nomadic pastoral lifestyle, watch dramatic jumping dances, visit the cattle enclosure that forms the heart of Maasai life, and browse beadwork crafted by the village women. Many visits directly fund community education and healthcare.
shortDescription: Visit a traditional Maasai homestead . warrior dances, cultural insights, and community-supporting beadwork.
highlights: Traditional warrior jumping dance performance
Tour of a Maasai manyatta (dung-and-stick homestead)
Fire-making demonstration using traditional methods
Beadwork shopping directly from the women artisans
Community fees support local education and health projects
notes: Choose community-run or lodge-partnered visits for a more authentic, respectful experience. Ask permission before photographing individuals. Prices vary . $20-30 is standard for group visits; $50 for more exclusive, in-depth experiences. Tipping is appreciated but not mandatory.

name: Lamu Old Town Walking Tour
description: Explore the narrow, winding streets of Lamu Old Town on a guided walking tour through East Africa's oldest and best-preserved Swahili settlement. Your guide leads you past ornately carved wooden doors, through bustling market alleys, into hidden courtyards, and along the waterfront where dhows are still built by hand using centuries-old techniques. Lamu's UNESCO-listed Old Town feels like stepping back in time.
shortDescription: Guided walk through Lamu's UNESCO Old Town . carved doors, dhow yards, and centuries of Swahili heritage.
highlights: Ornately carved Swahili doors . each tells a story
Working dhow boatyard where vessels are hand-built
Vibrant daily market with spices, fish, and textiles
Lamu's car-free streets navigated by donkeys
Rooftop views over the Old Town and harbour
notes: Dress modestly (covering shoulders and knees) out of respect for the predominantly Muslim community. Comfortable walking shoes are essential . streets are narrow and sometimes uneven. Early morning or late afternoon is best to avoid midday heat. Tipping your guide is customary.

name: Kazuri Beads Factory Tour
description: Tour the Kazuri Beads factory in Karen, where over 340 women . many single mothers . hand-shape, paint, and string colourful ceramic beads that are exported worldwide. Founded in 1977 as a social enterprise, Kazuri ('small and beautiful' in Swahili) offers free guided tours showing every step of the process, from raw clay to finished jewellery, followed by shopping in the factory outlet.
shortDescription: Free factory tour of Kazuri Beads . a women's social enterprise making hand-painted ceramic jewellery.
highlights: Watch artisans hand-shape and paint each bead
Learn the story of a pioneering women's social enterprise
Factory outlet with unique, handcrafted jewellery and pottery
Free guided tours . no entrance fee
Located in Karen . combine with Karen Blixen Museum and Giraffe Centre
notes: Open Monday-Saturday, approximately 8am-5pm. No booking needed for individual visitors; groups should call ahead. The factory outlet offers items at workshop prices. Located in the Karen suburb, easily combined with the Karen Blixen Museum and Giraffe Centre.

name: Kitengela Glass Art Studio
description: Visit the extraordinary Kitengela Hot Glass studio, a bohemian creative compound on the edge of Nairobi National Park where artists blow recycled glass into vibrant sculptures, mosaics, and functional art. The property itself is a living art installation . buildings, gardens, sculptures, and a swimming pool are all adorned with brilliant glass mosaic work. Visitors can try glass blowing and bead making.
shortDescription: Bohemian glass-blowing studio and art installation on the edge of Nairobi National Park . try your hand at glass art.
highlights: Watch artisans blow recycled glass into colourful sculptures
Hands-on glass blowing or bead-making workshops
Stunning mosaic-covered buildings and sculpture gardens
Adjacent to Nairobi National Park with occasional wildlife views
Unique, Instagrammable art installation setting
notes: Entry fee is approximately KES 500 ($4); glass blowing experiences cost more ($40-77). Call ahead to confirm opening hours and workshop availability. Located about 30 minutes south of Nairobi CBD. The property borders Nairobi National Park . you may spot giraffe and zebra from the garden.

name: Nairobi Food Tour (Budget)
description: Eat your way through Nairobi's vibrant street food scene on a budget-friendly walking food tour. A local guide leads you through bustling markets and street stalls sampling nyama choma (roasted meat), mutura (Kenyan sausage), samosas, chapati, mandazi (sweet doughnuts), and fresh tropical juices. This is how Nairobians really eat . flavourful, generous, and incredibly affordable.
shortDescription: Budget walking food tour through Nairobi's street food scene . nyama choma, samosas, and tropical juices.
operators: Local food tour guides (via Airbnb Experiences)
highlights: Sample 5-8 iconic Kenyan street foods
Visit local markets and hidden food stalls
Learn about Kenyan food culture from a local guide
Try nyama choma, mutura, and fresh tropical fruits
Incredibly affordable and authentic experience
notes: Come hungry . portions are generous. Let your guide know about dietary restrictions in advance. Street food is generally safe at busy, high-turnover stalls, but those with sensitive stomachs may want to stick to freshly cooked items. Carry small denomination notes for purchases.

name: Nairobi Food Tour (Premium)
description: Experience Nairobi's thriving contemporary food scene on a premium culinary tour that visits a curated selection of the city's best restaurants, artisan cafes, and hidden rooftop bars. Taste fusion dishes that blend traditional Kenyan flavours with international techniques, paired with Kenyan craft beers, wines from Naivasha, and artisan coffee from the Central Highlands.
shortDescription: Premium Nairobi food tour visiting top restaurants, artisan cafes, and craft beverage makers.
highlights: Visit 4-5 curated restaurants and bars
Contemporary Kenyan fusion cuisine and craft cocktails
Kenyan craft beer and Naivasha wine pairings
Meet chefs and learn about the New Kenyan Cuisine movement
Transport between venues included
notes: All food and drinks at the featured venues are included. Transport between locations is provided. Tours typically run from late morning into the afternoon or as evening experiences. Vegetarian and dietary alternatives can be arranged with advance notice. Smart-casual dress recommended for upscale venues.

name: Swahili Cooking Class
description: Learn the aromatic art of Swahili cooking in a hands-on class led by a local chef or home cook on the Kenya coast. Markets visits to source ingredients are followed by a lesson in preparing classics like biryani, pilau, coconut fish curry, bhajia, and mahamri. The class culminates in a communal feast of everything you have prepared . the most delicious souvenir of your trip.
shortDescription: Hands-on Swahili cooking class on the coast . market visit, spice lessons, and a communal feast.
highlights: Market visit to source fresh spices and ingredients
Learn 3-5 classic Swahili recipes from scratch
Spice identification . cardamom, turmeric, tamarind, and more
Communal feast of everything you prepare
Recipe cards to take home and recreate the dishes
notes: Classes range from budget home-kitchen experiences ($26) to upscale hotel-based classes ($65). Most include the market visit, ingredients, instruction, and the meal. Vegetarian, vegan, and halal options are easily accommodated. Wear comfortable clothing . kitchens can be warm. Most classes are conducted in English.

name: Coffee Farm Tour
description: Visit a working coffee farm in Kenya's Central Highlands and follow the journey of your morning cup from cherry to brew. Walk through lush coffee plantations, learn about the meticulous hand-picking and wet-processing methods that make Kenyan AA coffee world-famous, and participate in a cupping (tasting) session guided by a professional Q-grader.
shortDescription: Tour a working coffee farm in Kenya's highlands . from cherry picking to professional cupping session.
highlights: Walk through lush coffee plantations in the highlands
Learn hand-picking and wet-processing techniques
Professional cupping (tasting) session with a Q-grader
Understand what makes Kenyan AA coffee world-class
Purchase single-origin beans direct from the farm
notes: Located 30-90 minutes from Nairobi depending on the farm. Harvest season (October-December primary; June-July secondary) offers the fullest experience. Some tours include roasting demonstrations. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a light rain jacket in case of highland showers.

name: Kiambethu Tea Farm
description: Step back in time at Kiambethu Tea Farm, one of the oldest tea farms in Kenya, established in 1910 by the McDonell family who still run it today. The half-day visit includes a guided walk through emerald tea fields, a fascinating talk on the history and science of tea production, a multi-course farmhouse lunch, and a stroll through indigenous Mau Forest with colobus monkeys in the canopy.
shortDescription: Historic 1910 tea farm visit . tea field walks, production talk, farmhouse lunch, and colobus monkey forest.
highlights: Walk through rolling emerald tea fields
Fascinating talk on Kenya's tea history and production
Multi-course farmhouse lunch with home-grown produce
Indigenous forest walk with black-and-white colobus monkeys
Historic 1910 farm . one of Kenya's oldest
notes: Advance booking is essential . the farm accepts limited numbers daily. Located in Limuru, approximately 45 minutes from Nairobi. The visit includes tea, lunch, and the forest walk. Bring a light jacket . Limuru's highland altitude makes it cooler than Nairobi. Closed on Sundays.

name: Kericho Tea Walk
description: Explore the vast tea estates of Kericho, Kenya's tea capital in the western highlands, on a guided walk through some of the most productive tea fields in the world. The region's daily afternoon rains and rich volcanic soil produce the bright, coppery tea that forms the backbone of Kenya's export economy. Watch skilled pickers pluck the youngest leaves by hand.
shortDescription: Walk through Kenya's tea capital in Kericho . vast highland estates, hand-picking, and tea tasting.
highlights: Endless rolling tea fields as far as the eye can see
Watch hand-picking by skilled estate workers
Learn about Kenya's tea production . the world's largest exporter
Fresh highland air at 2,000m altitude
Extremely affordable experience
notes: Kericho is approximately 4-5 hours from Nairobi by road. The town rains almost every afternoon . bring waterproofs and plan walks for the morning. Accommodation is available at the heritage Kericho Tea Hotel. The experience is informal . arrange through your hotel or a local guide.

name: Carnivore Restaurant Experience
description: Feast at The Carnivore, Nairobi's legendary open-pit barbecue restaurant where Maasai swords deliver an endless parade of roasted meats directly to your table. The 'Beast of a Feast' concept serves rotating cuts of beef, lamb, pork ribs, chicken, and seasonal exotic meats (previously crocodile and ostrich) until you surrender by lowering the white flag at your table.
shortDescription: Nairobi's legendary meat feast . endless open-pit barbecue served on Maasai swords until you surrender.
highlights: All-you-can-eat open-pit barbecue
Meat carved at your table from Maasai swords
Signature 'surrender' white flag tradition
Live music and nightclub on weekends
Iconic Nairobi dining institution since 1980
notes: Reservations recommended, especially for weekends and holidays. The price covers the unlimited meat feast; drinks are separate. Vegetarian options are available but this is primarily a meat experience. Located on Langata Road near Wilson Airport. Friday and Saturday nights feature live music at the adjacent Simba Saloon.

name: Bush Breakfast or Dinner
description: Dine in the heart of the African bush at a specially prepared open-air table set against a backdrop of sweeping savanna, ancient kopjes, or riverbanks. Whether it is a champagne breakfast after a dawn game drive or a lantern-lit dinner under a canopy of stars, bush dining transforms a meal into a sensory immersion in the wilderness.
shortDescription: Open-air bush dining . champagne breakfast on the savanna or starlit dinner under African skies.
highlights: Elegantly set table in a wild bush setting
Champagne breakfast after a dawn game drive
Starlit dinner with lanterns and campfire
Gourmet multi-course menu by camp chefs
Private, intimate . usually for your party alone
notes: Bush dining is typically arranged by safari lodges and camps as a special add-on . request at booking. Costs vary widely: from $40 at mid-range camps to $150+ at ultra-luxury lodges. Weather-dependent . a backup indoor option is usually available. Inform the lodge of dietary requirements in advance.

name: Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage
description: Watch orphaned baby elephants being bottle-fed, mud-bathing, and playing at the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, the world's most successful elephant rescue and rehabilitation program. The one-hour public visit allows you to observe the tiny calves . many rescued from poaching or human-wildlife conflict . as their dedicated keepers describe each elephant's rescue story and personality.
shortDescription: Watch orphaned baby elephants bottle-feed and mud-bathe at the world's leading elephant rescue centre.
highlights: Baby elephants bottle-feeding and mud-bathing
Individual rescue stories told by dedicated keepers
Foster an orphan elephant from $50/year
Located inside Nairobi National Park
Supports Kenya's leading elephant conservation program
notes: Public visiting hours are 11am-12pm daily . arrive early as it gets crowded. Entry is $20 per adult, $5 per child. If combining with Nairobi National Park, the park fee ($80 non-resident) applies separately. Foster parent program allows private 5pm visits for $50 (limited availability). Booking online is recommended.

name: Giraffe Centre
description: Come face-to-face with endangered Rothschild's giraffes at the African Fund for Endangered Wildlife (AFEW) Giraffe Centre. An elevated platform brings you eye-to-eye with these gentle giants, allowing you to hand-feed them specially prepared pellets and even receive a famous 'giraffe kiss'. The centre is also home to warthogs, dik-dik, and a nature trail through adjacent forest.
shortDescription: Hand-feed and 'kiss' endangered Rothschild's giraffes at Nairobi's beloved Giraffe Centre.
highlights: Hand-feed Rothschild's giraffes from an elevated platform
The famous 'giraffe kiss' . a pellet from your lips
Learn about giraffe conservation and breeding programs
Nature trail through adjacent forest with warthogs and birds
Just 20 minutes from Nairobi CBD
notes: Open daily 9am-5pm. Entry is $15 for non-residents, KES 400 for residents. Pellets for feeding are included in the entry price. The centre is in Langata, easily combined with Karen Blixen Museum, Kazuri Beads, and Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage. Weekday mornings are less crowded.

name: Nairobi Safari Walk
description: Stroll through the Nairobi Safari Walk, a raised boardwalk and ground-level trail that winds through recreated Kenyan habitats . from savanna and wetland to forest . showcasing a wide range of wildlife including white rhino, bongo, cheetah, hyena, and a variety of primates and birds. It is a concentrated introduction to Kenya's biodiversity without needing a full safari.
shortDescription: Boardwalk through recreated Kenyan habitats with rhino, bongo, cheetah, and primates near Nairobi.
highlights: Close-up views of rare species like bongo and white rhino
Raised boardwalk through different habitat zones
Informative signage and education centre
Adjacent to Nairobi National Park (combine visits)
Accessible for all fitness levels including wheelchair users
notes: Open daily 8:30am-5:30pm. Entry is combined with the Animal Orphanage next door. Located on Langata Road adjacent to the main gate of Nairobi National Park. Allow 1.5-2 hours. The boardwalk is fully accessible. Photography is permitted throughout.

name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy
description: Visit Ol Pejeta Conservancy, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth (Najin and Fatu), the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa, and a chimpanzee sanctuary . the only one in Kenya. The 90,000-acre conservancy on the Laikipia Plateau supports all the Big Five and offers game drives, bush walks, night drives, and lion tracking with researchers.
shortDescription: Home to the last northern white rhinos and East Africa's largest black rhino sanctuary on the Laikipia Plateau.
highlights: Meet Najin and Fatu . the last two northern white rhinos
Largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa
Kenya's only chimpanzee sanctuary (Sweetwaters)
Big Five game drives on the Laikipia Plateau
Night drives and bush walks (not available in national parks)
notes: Conservancy fee is $110 per non-resident adult per day. Guided activities (game drives, lion tracking) are extra. Located near Nanyuki town, approximately 3.5 hours from Nairobi or a 30-minute flight to Nanyuki airstrip. Multiple accommodation options from budget to luxury within the conservancy.

name: Lake Baringo Birdwatching
description: Lake Baringo in the Rift Valley is one of Kenya's premier birdwatching destinations, with over 470 species recorded . one of the highest concentrations anywhere in Africa. A boat trip on the freshwater lake reveals fish eagles swooping for tilapia, Goliath herons stalking the shallows, and colonies of cormorants and pelicans on rocky islets, while the surrounding acacia woodland hides hornbills, starlings, and weavers.
shortDescription: World-class birdwatching on Lake Baringo . 470+ species including fish eagles and Goliath herons.
highlights: 470+ bird species . one of Africa's richest sites
Fish eagle calling and swooping demonstrations
Boat trip to rocky islets with nesting colonies
Goliath heron, kingfisher, and hornbill sightings
Combine with Lake Bogoria hot springs and flamingos
notes: A local bird guide is essential and affordable ($10-20 for a half-day). The boat trip ($8-15 per person) is the highlight. Migratory species from Europe and Asia are present September-April. Binoculars and a field guide (or birding app) are recommended. Lake Bogoria is just 30 minutes away . combine both in a two-day Rift Valley trip.

name: Lake Naivasha Boat Safari
description: Cruise the papyrus-fringed shores of Lake Naivasha on a boat safari through one of the Rift Valley's most scenic freshwater lakes. Hippos surface with thunderous snorts, African fish eagles cry from fever tree branches, and lily-covered bays harbour herons, jacanas, and kingfishers. The boat can land at Crescent Island for a walking safari among zebra and giraffe.
shortDescription: Boat safari on Lake Naivasha . hippos, fish eagles, and papyrus-fringed shores in the Rift Valley.
highlights: Hippo encounters at close range from the boat
African fish eagle sighting . Kenya's iconic raptor
Papyrus-fringed shoreline teeming with birdlife
Option to land at Crescent Island for a walking safari
Stunning Rift Valley scenery and fever tree forests
notes: Boat trips depart from several access points around the lake. Early morning (7-9am) is best for birdlife and calm water. The boat ride can be combined with Crescent Island ($33 entry + $20 boat) for a half-day experience. Lake Naivasha is 90 minutes from Nairobi . combine with Hell's Gate for a full day.

name: Kakamega Rainforest Walk
description: Walk through Kenya's only tropical rainforest . a remnant of the great Guineo-Congolian forest that once spanned the African continent. Kakamega Forest is a biodiversity hotspot harbouring over 330 bird species, 400 butterfly species, and primates including the De Brazza's monkey and blue monkey. Towering indigenous hardwoods create a dense, cathedral-like canopy.
shortDescription: Walk through Kenya's only tropical rainforest . rare primates, 330 bird species, and 400 butterfly species.
highlights: Kenya's only tropical rainforest . a unique ecosystem
330+ bird species including turacos and hornbills
400 butterfly species . highest diversity in Kenya
Primate sightings: blue monkey, De Brazza's monkey, colobus
Ancient hardwood trees and dense forest canopy
notes: Located in western Kenya, approximately 6 hours from Nairobi. A KWS ranger guide is mandatory and included in the entry fee. Wear waterproof boots . the forest floor can be muddy. Bring binoculars and a rain jacket. Early morning walks (6-9am) offer the best birding and primate sightings.

name: Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Walk
description: Explore the Arabuko-Sokoke Forest, the largest intact coastal forest in East Africa, on a guided nature walk through diverse habitats ranging from dense Brachystegia woodland to mixed forest and open grassland. The forest is a globally important biodiversity hotspot, home to six globally threatened bird species including Clarke's weaver and the Sokoke scops owl.
shortDescription: Guided walk through East Africa's largest coastal forest . rare birds, elephant shrews, and butterflies.
highlights: Six globally threatened bird species including Sokoke scops owl
Golden-rumped elephant shrew . one of the world's rarest mammals
Diverse forest types within a single walk
Butterfly-rich clearings . over 260 species recorded
Community-trained guides with expert knowledge
notes: The forest is located between Watamu and Malindi, making it an easy half-day excursion from either town. Night walks ($30+) are available for owling . the Sokoke scops owl is best seen after dark. Community guides from ASFGA are knowledgeable and affordable. Wear long trousers and closed shoes. Mosquito repellent is essential.

name: Nairobi National Park Game Drive
description: Experience the surreal sight of lions, rhinos, and giraffes roaming free with the Nairobi skyline shimmering in the background . the only place on Earth where this juxtaposition exists. Nairobi National Park, just 7 km from the city centre, is home to over 100 mammal species including the Big Four (no elephants) and is an important black rhino sanctuary.
shortDescription: Game drive in the world's only national park within a capital city . lions and rhinos with the Nairobi skyline behind.
bestSeason: Year-round (dry season Jun-Oct concentrates animals at water points)
highlights: Lions, rhinos, and buffalo with the Nairobi skyline behind
Black rhino sanctuary with growing population
Just 20 minutes from the city centre
Over 400 bird species . excellent birding
Combine with Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage (inside the park)
notes: Park entry is $80 for non-residents (paid via eCitizen portal or at the gate). Guided tours with transport cost an additional $50-100 per person. Early morning (6am gate opening) offers the best game viewing and coolest temperatures. Self-driving is permitted for those with a suitable vehicle. The park can be done as a half-day . ideal for travellers with limited time.

name: Karura Forest Walk
description: Escape the city in Karura Forest, a 1,000-hectare indigenous forest in the heart of Nairobi saved from development by the activism of Nobel laureate Wangari Maathai. Well-maintained trails wind through towering hardwood trees past waterfalls, caves, and a serene lake, offering jogging, cycling, and nature walking just minutes from the CBD.
shortDescription: 1,000-hectare indigenous forest oasis in Nairobi . waterfalls, caves, and trails saved by Wangari Maathai.
operators: Kenya Forest Service / Friends of Karura Forest
