highlights: Three waterfalls within the forest
Mau Mau caves . historical freedom fighter hideouts
15 km of walking, jogging, and cycling trails
Colobus monkeys, duikers, and bushbuck sightings
River Cafe restaurant for post-walk refreshments
notes: Open daily 6am-6pm. Entry is KES 800 ($6.50) for non-residents. Bikes can be rented at the gate. The River Cafe inside the forest is excellent for lunch or coffee. The forest is accessed via several gates . Limuru Road gate is most popular. Free guided nature walks are available on some weekends.

name: Lake Naivasha Combo Day Trip
description: Spend a full day exploring the Lake Naivasha area with a combination of a boat safari on the papyrus-fringed lake, a walking safari on Crescent Island, and cycling through Hell's Gate National Park. The region is just 90 minutes from Nairobi and packs an extraordinary variety of landscapes and wildlife into a single day.
shortDescription: Full-day Naivasha combo . boat safari, Crescent Island walk, and Hell's Gate cycling in one action-packed trip.
highlights: Boat safari with hippos and fish eagles
Walking safari among zebra and giraffe on Crescent Island
Cycling through Hell's Gate volcanic landscape
Three distinct experiences in one day
Just 90 minutes from Nairobi
notes: Most tour operators offer all-inclusive packages with transport from Nairobi, park fees, boat hire, and bike rental. Start early (7am departure) to fit everything in comfortably. Bring sunscreen, hat, and comfortable shoes. Pack a picnic or eat at Camp Carnelley's by the lake.

name: Crescent Island Walking Safari
description: Walk freely among wildlife on Crescent Island, a private wildlife sanctuary on Lake Naivasha where there are no predators and no fences. Zebra, giraffe, wildebeest, waterbuck, and gazelle graze within arm's reach as you stroll across the island's grassy plains . making it one of the closest and most intimate wildlife encounters possible in Kenya.
shortDescription: Walk among zebra, giraffe, and wildebeest with no fences and no vehicles on Crescent Island.
highlights: Walk within metres of giraffe, zebra, and wildebeest
No predators . safe for children and walking at your own pace
Film location for 'Out of Africa'
Boat transfer across Lake Naivasha included
Excellent birdwatching . fish eagles, pelicans, and herons
notes: Access is by boat only ($20 per person return from Camp Carnelley's or other jetties). Entry to the island is $33 per non-resident adult. No guide is strictly needed . you walk freely. Early morning or late afternoon offers the best light and cooler temperatures. Crescent Island featured in the film 'Out of Africa'.

name: Hell's Gate Day Trip
region: Hell's Gate National Park, Nakuru County
description: Spend a full day at Hell's Gate National Park combining cycling through its dramatic volcanic landscape, walking through the narrow Fischer's Tower gorge with natural hot springs, and climbing the towering cliffs. The park . one of only two in Kenya where you can walk and cycle . offers a remarkably active and affordable day out from Nairobi.
shortDescription: Full-day Hell's Gate adventure . cycling past wildlife, gorge walking, rock climbing, and hot springs.
highlights: Cycle through dramatic volcanic cliffs alongside wildlife
Fischer's Tower gorge walk with natural hot springs
Rock climbing on the towering basalt columns
Geothermal steam vents and volcanic formations
Affordable . one of Kenya's best-value national parks
notes: Park entry $26 (non-resident). Bike rental $5-10 at the gate. A guide for the gorge walk costs an additional $5-10. Flash floods can occur in the gorge after heavy rain . check conditions with rangers. Located 90 minutes from Nairobi. Combine with Lake Naivasha for a full day.

name: Fourteen Falls
description: Visit Fourteen Falls on the Athi River near Thika, where the river cascades over a wide, horseshoe-shaped basalt shelf creating fourteen distinct waterfalls during the rainy season. The surrounding tropical vegetation, mist, and thundering water create a refreshing natural spectacle just an hour from Nairobi. Local guides offer walks to viewing platforms and boat rides to the base of the falls.
shortDescription: Fourteen cascading waterfalls on the Athi River near Thika . most dramatic during the rainy season.
bestSeason: April to June (rainy season . fullest flow)
operators: Local community guides at the falls
highlights: Fourteen distinct waterfalls on a wide basalt shelf
Most dramatic during the long rains (April-June)
Boat ride to the base of the falls
Lush tropical vegetation and cooling mist
Just 1 hour from Nairobi . easy half-day trip
notes: The falls are most impressive after heavy rains (April-June); during dry season, flow may be reduced. A local guide is recommended for safety near the slippery rocks. Entry is approximately KES 2,500 ($20). Swimming is not recommended due to strong currents. Combine with Thika town for a Kenyan coffee and fruit market experience.

name: Paradise Lost
description: Discover Paradise Lost, a hidden recreational park in Kiambu featuring a stunning underground cave, a waterfall, boating lake, and manicured gardens. The cave system is the highlight . descend into the cool underground chambers where stalactites and underground pools create an otherworldly atmosphere. Above ground, enjoy boat rides, fishing, and picnicking in a lush tropical setting.
shortDescription: Hidden cave system, waterfall, and boating lake in Kiambu . a family-friendly escape near Nairobi.
highlights: Underground cave with stalactites and pools
Waterfall and scenic nature trails
Boating lake and fishing pond
Spacious picnic grounds and playground
Just 30 minutes from Nairobi CBD
notes: Entry is KES 500-2,000 ($4-16) depending on age and included activities. The cave descent requires moderate fitness . some sections have steep steps. Bring a light jacket for the cool cave interior. Weekends can be busy . arrive early for a quieter experience. Bring your own picnic or buy food at the on-site restaurant.

name: Olorgesailie Prehistoric Site
description: Step back 900,000 years at Olorgesailie Prehistoric Site, one of the most significant Stone Age archaeological sites in Africa. Discovered by Louis and Mary Leakey, the open-air museum displays thousands of hand axes and cleavers exactly where they were found on the ancient lake bed. The surrounding Rift Valley landscape remains much as it was when early humans lived here.
shortDescription: 900,000-year-old Stone Age site discovered by the Leakeys . hand axes preserved where they were found.
highlights: 900,000-year-old Acheulean hand axes in situ
Discovered by Louis and Mary Leakey
Open-air museum on an ancient lake bed
Fascinating guided tour by resident curator
Remote Rift Valley setting . feel the vastness of time
notes: Located approximately 1.5 hours south of Nairobi on the road to Magadi. The site is managed by the National Museums of Kenya. A guided tour by the resident curator/guide is included and highly recommended. Bring sun protection . the site is exposed and hot. There are no restaurants nearby . bring water and snacks.

name: Giraffe Manor Stay
description: Stay at Giraffe Manor, one of the world's most Instagrammed hotels, where resident Rothschild's giraffes poke their heads through the windows at breakfast, join you on the terrace for afternoon tea, and stroll the manicured grounds of this 1930s manor house. With just 12 rooms, the experience is intimate, exclusive, and utterly unforgettable.
shortDescription: Iconic boutique hotel where giraffes join you for breakfast through the window . just 12 rooms in a 1930s manor.
highlights: Giraffes poking their heads through your bedroom window
Breakfast with giraffes on the terrace
1930s Scottish hunting lodge architecture and decor
Just 12 rooms . deeply intimate and exclusive
All-inclusive: meals, drinks, and Giraffe Centre visit
notes: Book 6-12 months in advance . Giraffe Manor is one of the hardest reservations in Africa. Rates are all-inclusive (accommodation, meals, house drinks, laundry, and excursions). Located in Langata, 20 minutes from Nairobi CBD. Owned by The Safari Collection, which also operates Sala's Camp and Solio Lodge.

name: Fly-In Safari
region: Nationwide (Wilson Airport to all major parks)
description: Skip the long road transfers and fly directly to Kenya's top safari destinations from Wilson Airport in Nairobi aboard scheduled or charter light aircraft. In under an hour, you can be landing on a bush airstrip in the Maasai Mara, Samburu, Lewa, or Amboseli . maximising your time in the bush and minimising travel fatigue.
shortDescription: Fly-in safari transfers from Nairobi to bush airstrips . skip the drive and maximise game-viewing time.
highlights: Arrive at the Mara in 45 minutes instead of 5 hours by road
Aerial views of the Rift Valley, lakes, and wildlife
Bush airstrip landings . an adventure in themselves
Scheduled and private charter options available
15 kg soft-bag luggage limit (pack light!)
notes: Flights depart from Wilson Airport (not JKIA). Luggage is limited to 15 kg in a soft bag . no hard suitcases. Scheduled flights run daily to the Mara, Samburu, Lewa, Amboseli, and Lamu. Charter flights can reach any airstrip in Kenya. Book seats early during peak season (Jul-Oct). Prices quoted are per person return on scheduled services.

name: Private Conservancy Safari
description: Stay in an exclusive lodge or tented camp within a private conservancy bordering a national reserve, where visitor numbers are strictly limited and activities unavailable in public parks . night drives, walking safaris, off-road driving, and bush dinners . are all on the menu. Private conservancies offer the most intimate and flexible safari experience in Kenya.
shortDescription: Exclusive safari in a private conservancy . limited guests, night drives, walking safaris, and off-road freedom.
highlights: Strictly limited visitor numbers . often exclusive to one lodge
Night drives, walking safaris, and off-road driving
Bush dinners and sundowners in private settings
Direct community benefit . conservancy fees fund local livelihoods
Some of Africa's finest luxury lodges and camps
notes: Conservancy rates are typically all-inclusive: accommodation, meals, house drinks, laundry, conservancy fees, and all activities. Most are accessed by light aircraft from Nairobi (45-60 min). Children's policies vary . some camps are adults-only or have minimum age requirements. Book 3-6 months ahead for peak season.

name: Private Island Stay Lamu
description: Escape to a private island hideaway in the Lamu Archipelago, where barefoot luxury meets centuries-old Swahili culture. Stay in exquisitely designed villas with private pools, dine on freshly caught seafood under the stars, and spend your days sailing, snorkeling, and exploring the UNESCO World Heritage town of Lamu. The archipelago's car-free, time-forgotten pace is the ultimate digital detox.
shortDescription: Barefoot luxury on a private island in the Lamu Archipelago . villas, dhow sailing, and Swahili culture.
highlights: Private villa with pool overlooking the Indian Ocean
Dhow sailing, snorkeling, and deep-sea fishing
Freshly caught seafood and Swahili cuisine
Day trips to UNESCO Lamu Old Town
Car-free island life . total relaxation
notes: Lamu is reached by flight from Nairobi (1.5 hours to Lamu/Manda Airport) or from Malindi. Boat transfers to specific islands are arranged by the property. The archipelago is predominantly Muslim . dress modestly when visiting Lamu Town. Rainy season (April-June) sees lower prices but rougher seas.

name: Exclusive Bush Dining
description: Dine under the African sky at an elegantly styled table set in a dramatic bush location . atop a kopje, beside a river, or on an open plain. Exclusive bush dining is the art of transforming wilderness into fine dining, with multi-course menus, silver service, candlelight, and the soundtrack of the African night. Many lodges offer this as a private experience for just your party.
shortDescription: Private fine dining under the stars in a dramatic bush setting . multi-course menus and silver service.
highlights: Elegantly set table in a wild, dramatic location
Multi-course gourmet menu by camp chefs
Private . usually just your party
Lanterns, candles, and campfire ambiance
Sounds of the African night as your soundtrack
notes: Arrange through your safari lodge . most offer this as an add-on. Costs vary widely based on lodge tier. Inform the kitchen of dietary needs in advance. Weather backup plans are standard. Best during clear, moonless nights for stargazing. Combine with a night game drive for the full experience.

name: Luxury Yoga Retreat
description: Unwind on a luxury yoga retreat in one of Kenya's most beautiful settings . from beachfront studios overlooking the Indian Ocean to highland lakeside pavilions. Programs range from weekend getaways to two-week immersions, combining daily yoga and meditation with spa treatments, healthy cuisine, and optional adventures like snorkeling, nature walks, or safari day trips.
shortDescription: Luxury yoga retreat in stunning Kenyan settings . daily practice, spa, healthy cuisine, and optional adventures.
highlights: Daily yoga and meditation in stunning natural settings
Spa treatments and holistic wellness programs
Healthy, locally sourced cuisine . often organic
Optional adventures: snorkeling, safari, nature walks
Small groups for personalised attention
notes: Retreats cater to all levels from complete beginners to advanced practitioners. Price range reflects the wide spectrum from budget beachside retreats to ultra-luxury spa resorts. Bring your own yoga mat or borrow from the venue. Some retreats include airport transfers. Book well ahead for peak-season retreats (Jan-Feb, Jul-Aug).

name: Safari Lodge Spa Treatment
description: Indulge in a spa treatment between game drives at one of Kenya's luxury safari lodges. Many bush spas use locally sourced ingredients . Maasai herbs, honey, coffee, and essential oils . in massages, facials, and body wraps administered in open-air treatment rooms overlooking the savanna. It is wellness with a wild view.
shortDescription: Bush spa treatments with savanna views . local herbs, honey, and essential oils between game drives.
highlights: Open-air treatment rooms with savanna or river views
Locally sourced ingredients . honey, herbs, coffee
Perfect midday activity between morning and evening drives
Professional therapists trained in African and international techniques
Couple's treatments available at most lodges
notes: Book treatments in advance as bush lodge spas have limited therapists. Midday (11am-3pm) is the ideal time when game viewing is quieter. Treatments are typically charged separately from all-inclusive rates. Some lodges include a complimentary treatment in the room rate . check when booking.

name: Coastal Yoga Retreat
description: Reconnect with yourself on a yoga retreat along Kenya's Indian Ocean coast, where the rhythm of the waves sets the pace for daily practice. Sessions take place in open-air studios with ocean views, complemented by meditation, breathwork, and optional Ayurvedic or Thai massage treatments. Healthy coastal cuisine . fresh fish, tropical fruits, and Swahili flavours . nourishes from within.
shortDescription: Beachfront yoga retreat with ocean-view studios, meditation, massage, and healthy coastal cuisine.
highlights: Daily yoga in ocean-view open-air studios
Meditation and breathwork sessions
Ayurvedic or Thai massage treatments
Healthy cuisine with fresh seafood and tropical fruits
Optional beach walks, snorkeling, and dhow sailing
notes: All levels welcome . from absolute beginners to advanced practitioners. Price varies significantly with accommodation standard: budget beach cottages are at the lower end; luxury boutique villas at the top. Most retreats are on the south coast (Diani) or in the Lamu Archipelago. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

name: Lake Bogoria Hot Springs
description: Soak in the geothermal hot springs on the shores of Lake Bogoria, a Rift Valley soda lake famous for its boiling geysers, steaming fumaroles, and vast flamingo congregations. The hot springs range from scalding-hot geysers to warm pools perfect for bathing, all set against a dramatic backdrop of sheer Rift Valley cliffs and the pink-tinged alkaline lake.
shortDescription: Geothermal hot springs and flamingo-filled soda lake in the Rift Valley . natural spa meets raw geology.
highlights: Natural geothermal hot springs for bathing
Boiling geysers and steaming fumaroles
Greater flamingo congregations along the lake shore
Dramatic Rift Valley escarpment backdrop
Greater kudu . one of the few places to see them in Kenya
notes: The geysers can be dangerously hot . stay on marked paths and test water temperature carefully. The bathing pools are distinct from the boiling geysers. Located about 4 hours north of Nairobi. Park entry is approximately $50 for non-residents. Combine with Lake Baringo (30 minutes away) for a two-day Rift Valley trip.

name: Olkaria Geothermal Spa
description: Relax in naturally heated geothermal pools at the Olkaria Geothermal Spa, located within Hell's Gate National Park near Lake Naivasha. The pools are heated by the same volcanic activity that powers Kenya's largest geothermal power station nearby. It is a unique chance to soak in warm, mineral-rich water surrounded by the park's dramatic volcanic landscape.
shortDescription: Geothermally heated mineral pools inside Hell's Gate National Park . volcanic relaxation near Naivasha.
priceDisplay: $18 per person (spa entry; park fee separate)
highlights: Naturally heated geothermal swimming pools
Mineral-rich water from volcanic aquifers
Located inside Hell's Gate National Park
Combine with cycling and gorge walking in the park
Affordable and family-friendly
notes: Spa entry is approximately KES 2,000-2,500 ($18) on top of the Hell's Gate park entry fee ($26). Bring a swimsuit and towel . rental is limited. The water is warm (not hot) and suitable for children. The spa has changing rooms and basic facilities. Weekends can be crowded . visit on weekdays for a quieter experience.

name: KICC Conference Venue
description: Host your conference or corporate event at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi's landmark venue and one of Africa's most recognisable buildings. The centre offers a range of conference halls, exhibition spaces, and boardrooms accommodating from 20 to 5,000 delegates, with a rooftop helipad and panoramic viewing deck offering sweeping views across the city to the national park.
shortDescription: Nairobi's landmark convention centre . conference halls for 20-5,000 delegates with rooftop city views.
priceDisplay: Varies by event size and requirements
highlights: Iconic Nairobi landmark . immediately recognisable
Multiple halls accommodating 20 to 5,000 delegates
Rooftop viewing deck with panoramic city views
Central CBD location with easy access
Full AV, catering, and event management support
notes: Contact KICC directly for venue hire pricing . rates depend on hall size, duration, and services required. The viewing deck is open to the public ($5 entry) and offers one of the best views of Nairobi. Located in the heart of the CBD, easily accessible by public transport. Multiple international hotels within walking distance.

name: Corporate Team Building
description: Energise your team with a corporate team-building day featuring white-water rafting on the Tana River, zip-lining, ropes courses, paintball, and problem-solving challenges set in the scenic outdoors. Professional facilitators design programs around your organisation's goals, from leadership development to communication and trust-building, all wrapped in adrenaline-fueled fun.
shortDescription: Action-packed corporate team building . rafting, zip-lining, and facilitated challenges in the Kenyan outdoors.
highlights: White-water rafting, zip-lining, and ropes courses
Professional facilitation tailored to corporate objectives
Scenic outdoor settings 1-2 hours from Nairobi
Full catering and event logistics handled
Customisable programs for groups of 10-200+
notes: Most venues offer full-day packages including activities, lunch, and facilitation. Transport from Nairobi is usually extra. Minimum group size is typically 10 people. Tailor activities to the group's fitness level . not everyone needs to raft. Wet season (Apr-May) may limit some activities. Book 2-4 weeks ahead for large groups.

name: Bush Conference Retreat
description: Combine business with safari by hosting a conference, board retreat, or incentive trip at a luxury bush lodge. Many of Kenya's top safari properties offer dedicated conference facilities . boardrooms, Wi-Fi, AV equipment, and breakout spaces . alongside world-class game drives, bush dining, and spa treatments. The result: productive meetings and unforgettable team experiences.
shortDescription: Conference and board retreat at a luxury bush lodge . boardroom meetings by day, game drives by evening.
highlights: Dedicated conference facilities in the bush
Game drives before and after meetings
Bush dinners and sundowners for team bonding
Spa treatments during break sessions
Fly-in access for time efficiency
notes: Lodge conference rates typically include full board, drinks, game drives, and meeting room hire. Wi-Fi is available at most lodges but bandwidth is limited . not suitable for heavy video conferencing. Fly-in transfers from Nairobi (45-60 min) save time vs. road. Book 2-3 months ahead, especially for exclusive-use buyouts.

name: Golf Experience
description: Play a round of golf at one of Kenya's scenic courses, from the colonial-era fairways of the Karen Country Club and Muthaiga Golf Club in Nairobi to the dramatic Rift Valley setting of the Great Rift Valley Lodge course near Naivasha and the tropical coastal course at Vipingo Ridge. Kenya's highland climate and year-round green conditions make for excellent golfing.
shortDescription: Play scenic golf courses in Nairobi, the Rift Valley, and the coast . highland climate and year-round green fairways.
operators: Great Rift Valley Lodge & Golf Resort
highlights: Scenic courses with wildlife on the fairways
Year-round green conditions in the highlands
Colonial-era club atmospheres at Karen and Muthaiga
Rift Valley and coastal course options
Club and equipment hire available at most courses
notes: Green fees range from $35-62 for visitors; caddy fees and club hire are extra. Some clubs require prior introduction . check guest policies. Kenya's altitude (Nairobi is at 1,700m) means the ball travels further than at sea level. Collared shirts and golf shoes are typically required. Booking a tee time in advance is recommended.

name: Running Camp Iten
description: Train alongside world-champion marathon and track athletes at a running camp in Iten, the legendary 'Home of Champions' perched at 2,400m on the edge of the Rift Valley escarpment. Programs range from two-week structured camps to drop-in training, with coached morning runs on red-dirt trails, access to tracks, altitude training benefits, and the chance to learn from the greatest distance runners on Earth.
shortDescription: Train at altitude with world-champion runners in Iten . Kenya's legendary 'Home of Champions'.
highlights: Train at 2,400m altitude for natural performance gains
Run alongside Olympic and World Championship athletes
Coached morning sessions on legendary red-dirt trails
Rift Valley escarpment views from training routes
Cultural immersion in Kenya's running heartland
notes: A base level of running fitness is required . most camps expect participants to run at least 30-40 km per week. Altitude adjustment takes 3-5 days . expect initial performance to drop. Camps typically include accommodation, meals, coaching, and some excursions. Iten is approximately 5-6 hours from Nairobi by road or a flight to Eldoret (1 hour) plus a 40-minute drive.

name: Lewa Safari Marathon
description: Run a marathon (or half marathon) through a wildlife conservancy teeming with rhinos, elephants, zebra, and giraffe at the legendary Lewa Safari Marathon. Held annually in late June, this is one of the world's most unique races . armed rangers line the route for runner safety, and the terrain includes red-dirt tracks, river crossings, and challenging hills at 1,600m altitude. Proceeds directly fund wildlife conservation.
shortDescription: Run a marathon through a rhino conservancy alongside wildlife . one of the world's most unique races.
highlights: Run alongside rhinos, elephants, and giraffe
Armed rangers for runner safety throughout the course
Full marathon and half marathon distances available
All proceeds fund wildlife and community conservation
One of National Geographic's 'Top 10 Marathons in the World'
notes: The 2026 race is scheduled for June 27. Registration opens months in advance and sells out . book early. The course is hilly and at altitude (1,600m) . train accordingly. Entry fee includes race entry, camping at Lewa, and meals. Many runners combine the race with a safari holiday. Fundraising commitments apply for some entry tiers.

name: Kenya Wildlife Marathon
description: Race through Tsavo West National Park on the Kenya Wildlife Marathon, a spectacular off-road race set against the backdrop of volcanic landscapes, acacia woodland, and the vast expanse of one of Africa's largest wildlife parks. The race offers full marathon, half marathon, and shorter distances, with wildlife sightings along the route adding a truly wild dimension to the running experience.
shortDescription: Off-road marathon through Tsavo West National Park . volcanic landscapes and wildlife along the route.
highlights: Run through a major wildlife national park
Volcanic landscapes and acacia woodland course
Full marathon, half marathon, and shorter distances
Support wildlife conservation with your entry
Unique race medal and finisher's experience
notes: The 2026 race is scheduled for May 24. Entry details and pricing are typically announced 3-6 months before the event . check the official website. The course is challenging with off-road terrain and potential heat. Previous marathon or trail running experience is strongly recommended. Accommodation and transport packages are usually offered by the organisers.
